chapters.2.meaning: Families name their earlier homes. Priests without proof must wait before eating the most holy food.
chapters.3.meaning: Older people remember the earlier temple and weep. Others cheer as the new foundation is laid.
chapters.4.meaning: The chapter moves between different kings. Some later letters concern the city's walls instead of temple work.
chapters.6.meaning: The king pays for work and offerings from taxes. The feast includes people who leave other gods.
chapters.9.meaning: Ezra recalls earlier sins that sent Israel into exile. He fears losing the small group that survived.
people.shimshai.meaning: He writes accusations with Rehum. They ask the king to stop work in Jerusalem.
people.haggai.meaning: He encourages the people to rebuild. His own prophetic book records more of his teaching.
people.hashabiah.meaning: He joins the Levites who travel with Ezra and carry temple gifts.
people.eleazar-phinehas.meaning: He helps weigh the returned gifts in Jerusalem. His father is named Phinehas.
people.shecaniah-jehiel.meaning: He proposes sending away foreign wives and children. Ezra then calls the leaders to make a promise.
people.jehohanan-eliashib.meaning: Ezra goes to his room to mourn and fast after the assembly.
chapters.1.meaning: Neighbors give gold, animals, and supplies. Their gifts help families prepare for the return.
chapters.2.summary: A list names returning families and temple workers. Some priests must prove their family line.
chapters.5.title: Prophets encourage work as officials ask questions
chapters.5.summary: Haggai and Zechariah encourage rebuilding. Tattenai asks for proof of Cyrus's order, and the leaders explain their work.
chapters.5.meaning: The builders recall Sheshbazzar's earlier foundation work. Officials seek written proof of the king's permission.
chapters.7.title: Ezra studies the law and receives royal support
chapters.8.title: Prayer, travel, and the care of temple gifts
chapters.8.meaning: Ezra chooses people to guard the gifts. They must hand over the same weight they received.
chapters.9.title: Ezra prays about the mixed marriages
chapters.9.summary: Leaders report marriages with women from other nations. Ezra tears his robe and begins a prayer.
people.cyrus.role: Persian king who permits temple rebuilding
people.jeremiah.role: Earlier prophet remembered in Cyrus's announcement
people.nebuchadnezzar.role: Babylonian king who took people and temple vessels
people.jeshua-priest.role: Priest who helps lead the returning people
people.returning-families.role: Families and workers named in the return list
people.moses.role: Earlier leader remembered through God's law
people.asaph-singer.role: Earlier singer whose descendants serve at the temple
people.darius-ezra.role: Persian king who supports the temple's completion
people.ahasuerus-ezra.role: Persian king who receives an accusation
people.artaxerxes-ezra.role: Persian king who receives letters and sends Ezra
people.mithredath-writer.role: Man named in a letter against Jerusalem
people.shimshai.role: Writer of a letter against Jerusalem
people.tattenai.role: Governor who asks about the temple work
people.shethar-bozenai.role: Official who joins Tattenai's questions about the temple
people.ezra.role: Priest who studies and teaches God's law
people.aaron.role: Earlier priest whose descendants serve at the temple
people.hashabiah.role: Levite who helps carry temple gifts
people.meremoth.role: Priest who weighs the gifts in Jerusalem
people.foreign-wives-children.role: Women and children affected by the separation plan
people.shecaniah-jehiel.role: Man who proposes sending away foreign wives and children
people.jehohanan-eliashib.role: Man whose room Ezra enters to fast
people.marriage-objectors.role: Men who oppose the plan in this translation
people.shabbethai.role: Levite who stands with men opposing the plan
chapters.6.title: The king's order, the temple, and Passover
chapters.10.meaning: Rain and the many cases delay the work. Leaders set times to examine each household.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me studies the temple's opening and the people's joy.
chapters.8.summary: Ezra gathers travelers and asks Iddo to send temple workers. They pray before leaving and count the gifts when they arrive.
people.cyrus.relations: He orders the temple rebuilt and returns its vessels.
people.cyrus.meaning: His order lets families return and rebuild the temple.
people.jeremiah.meaning: The opening links Cyrus's order with Jeremiah's earlier message.
people.nebuchadnezzar.meaning: He had taken people and vessels from Jerusalem. Their return helps repair that earlier loss.
people.jeshua-priest.meaning: He leads offerings and helps rebuild the temple with Zerubbabel.
people.moses.meaning: The builders follow the law Moses gave Israel. Ezra later studies and teaches that law.
people.david.meaning: Temple singers follow David's instructions. Ezra's travel list also includes a man from David's family.
people.rehum-chancellor.meaning: He writes accusations against Jerusalem. The king's answer lets him stop the builders.
people.zechariah-prophet.meaning: He joins Haggai in encouraging the temple's builders.
people.tattenai.meaning: He asks the builders who gave them permission. He sends their answer to the king.
people.ezra.meaning: He gathers people and gifts for the temple. He later asks men to send away foreign wives and children.
people.aaron.meaning: Ezra's family list connects him with Aaron, Israel's first high priest.
people.sherebiah.meaning: Iddo sends him with relatives to join Ezra. He helps guard gifts during the journey.
people.noadiah-ezra.meaning: He works beside Meremoth, Eleazar, and Jozabad when the gifts arrive.
people.marriage-objectors.meaning: Our reading text says they oppose the plan. The Church Bible's main text describes work on the case.
people.shabbethai.meaning: He supports Jonathan and Jahzeiah during the debate.
chapters.2.lds: The Seminary introduction describes the families returning from exile, or forced life abroad. What do their gifts help rebuild?
